did_you_know.text: Did you know? Solomon organized a large workforce to build the temple: 70,000 carriers, 80,000 stonecutters in the hills, and 3,600 supervisors.
Did you know? Solomon approached Huram, king of Tyre, and reminded him of the cooperation between Huram and his father David, especially the shipment of cedar from Lebanon to build David’s palace.

Did you know? Solomon explained that the purpose of the temple was to carry out the worship of the LORD: burning incense, offering daily burnt offerings and offerings on appointed occasions, and maintaining Israel’s worship practices.
Did you know? Although the temple is described as great and magnificent, Solomon emphasizes that the greatness of the building cannot encompass the greatness of God.
Did you know? Solomon declared that the heavens—even the highest heavens—cannot contain the LORD; therefore, the temple was not a place that confined God, but a place dedicated to his worship.
Did you know? Solomon asked Huram to send a skilled craftsman experienced in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue yarn, as well as in carving and engraving.
Did you know? The building materials Solomon requested included cedar, cypress, and algum wood from Lebanon, because Huram’s workers knew how to cut and process the trees of Lebanon.
Did you know? Solomon offered to provide the workers from Tyre with regular payment consisting of wheat, barley, wine, and oil, in large quantities measured in kors and baths.
Did you know? Huram blessed the LORD and acknowledged that Solomon was a wise son given to David to build the house of the LORD and his royal palace.

Did you know? Solomon counted 153,600 resident foreigners living in the land of Israel and assigned them as follows: 70,000 carriers, 80,000 stonecutters, and 3,600 supervisors; the numbers add up to the total.
